iconicAnchor.label: Berlin Dada photomontage and chance collage
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Hannah Hoch, Kurt Schwitters, Jean Arp, and the Dada movement
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: MoMA connects Dada collage to chance, accident, improvisation, mass-media fragments, anti-rational critique, and deliberately disruptive juxtaposition.

sources.title: Chance Creations: Collage, Photomontage, and Assemblage
supports: Dada artists used chance, accident, and improvisation to challenge rational order.
Magazine and newspaper imagery became raw material for distorted, critical photomontage.

sources.title: DADA at MoMA
supports: The movement joined abstraction, collage, photomontage, performance, and media pranks rather than maintaining one polished style.
Dada's response to machine culture supports the guide's mechanical fragments and ruptured scale.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches collage, rough, layered, improvised, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/dada-collage/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
